en: Oṃ, homage to Jambhala!
You whose pair of feet are saluted by Indra, Agni, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the Sun.
O Blessed One, cast upon me, who am suffering, your lotus-like gaze. ||1||
You are satisfied with a mere handful of water;
tell me, who else is more compassionate than you? You have disregarded all methods of formal worship.
Those like you are generally difficult to find. ||2||
Having searched and searched with effort out of compassion, you somehow behold those fallen into miserable rebirths right before you and bring them happiness.
Why do you not [look upon] me with my face soiled by tears? ||3||
Alas, even while you stand with your bow of compassion fully drawn, how is it that people [still suffer]?
O Blessed One, it is being plundered by the army of thieves that are unavoidable sufferings. ||4||
O Lord, for the sake of the welfare of sentient beings, you indeed rain down a shower of various jewels and gems; upon me, who am solely devoted to your virtues, [you rain them down].
Not even drops spread forth; how then [could there be anything else]? ||5||
While you exist, calamities burn me all the more, like the flames of a fire that has taken up the burden of the three worlds.
Whither has the cow of compassion gone? ||6||
Even the auspicious vase, the wish-fulfilling tree, and the thought-gem are insentient;
yet even they bring happiness to sentient beings.
How much more so, then, has the Blessed One been accepted out of compassion? ||7||
Whoever grasps your name, O Jambhala, Lord of the Waters, for even a moment,
in that person you shall dwell like a bed of lotuses.
The goddess Lakṣmī, with her radiant lotus, dwells therein.
O you whose existence has been destroyed, by the merit that arises from this wailing performed before you,
may [it] grant the desired fruit.
O Blessed One, may people be born like you.
Thus ends the Jambhala-stotra composed by Candragomin.
